quests.hint: Three beats: TICK, SELL, FAST.
quests.explanation: English rhythm is stress-timed: stressed syllables come at fairly regular intervals. Here TICK, SELL and FAST make three beats.
quests.textToSpeak: Tickets sell fast.
quests.instruction: Tap the beats as you listen, then repeat in the same rhythm.

quests.hint: Keep the same three beats; squeeze 'the' and 'are'.
quests.explanation: There are more syllables than in the previous quest, but the beats stay TICK, SELL and FAST. 'The', '-ets are' and '-ing' are squeezed to fit.
quests.textToSpeak: The tickets are selling fast.
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Still three main beats; squash 'have been' and 'really'.
quests.explanation: Even more small words, yet the beat pattern is still TICK, SELL, FAST. Squeezing 'have been' and '-ing really' stops your speech sounding word-by-word.
quests.textToSpeak: The tickets have been selling really fast.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the beat.

quests.hint: Beats on SEND, FILE and FRI-day.
quests.explanation: 'Could you', 'the' and 'to me by' are squeezed between the beats on SEND, FILE and FRI-day. The result is a polite request that still sounds brisk.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you send the file to me by Friday?
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on WAIT, RE-SULTS and TEST.
quests.explanation: The beats are WAIT, RE-sults and TEST. 'For the' and 'of the' are compressed to almost nothing.
quests.textToSpeak: We're waiting for the results of the test.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on ASK, BRING, KEYS and OF-fice.
quests.explanation: Four content words carry beats: ASK, BRING, KEYS and OF-fice. 'To the' appears twice and should be quick both times.
quests.textToSpeak: Ask Sam to bring the keys to the office.
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same bounce and timing as the model.

quests.hint: Give each digit a steady beat; keep the first part light.
quests.explanation: Digits are all content words, so each gets an even beat. Keep the tempo steady and let the last digit fall.
quests.textToSpeak: Your booking number is four, two, seven, nine.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on TAKE, TWELVE, BUS, BA-ker STREET.
quests.explanation: Directions have a steady beat on the key words. 'Number twelve' and 'Baker Street' are both spoken as compact units.
quests.textToSpeak: Take the number twelve bus to Baker Street.
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.hint: Keep the beats even: ONE, THREE, EIGHT; MA-drid; TWEN-ty.
quests.explanation: Flight numbers are read digit by digit with an even beat, and then Madrid and gate twenty each form a separate chunk.
quests.textToSpeak: It's flight one-three-eight to Madrid, gate twenty.
quests.instruction: Tap the beats as you listen, then repeat in the same rhythm.

quests.hint: Beats on LOVE-ly, LIT-tle, BAKE-ry, COR-ner.
quests.explanation: 'Lovely' and 'little' are adjectives, so each gets a beat before the noun, and 'around the' is squeezed: LOVE-ly LIT-tle BAKE-ry, a-ROUND the COR-ner.
quests.textToSpeak: That's a lovely little bakery around the corner.
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.hint: Beats on REAL-ly, USE-ful, PIECE and SOFT-ware.
quests.explanation: The stress falls on REAL-ly, USE-ful, PIECE and SOFT-ware. 'Of' reduces to /əv/ and slips between beats.
quests.textToSpeak: It's a really useful piece of software.
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on RATH-er, LONG, TIR-ing, JOUR-ney.
quests.explanation: Two adjectives joined by a weak 'and' create an even rhythm: LONG and TIR-ing. Keep 'and' as /ən/ so the beats stay close together.
quests.textToSpeak: We had a rather long and tiring journey.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the beat.

quests.hint: Beats on IS-n't, BAD and LOOKS.
quests.explanation: In this fixed comparison, 'as' is weak, and only BAD and LOOKS carry beats. Speaking each word evenly would sound robotic.
quests.textToSpeak: It isn't as bad as it looks.
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on WOULD-n't, THOUGHT and THAT.
quests.explanation: 'Have' and 'of' reduce, so the phrase sounds like 'wouldn't-əv THOUGHT-əv THAT'. The beats are WOULD-n't, THOUGHT and THAT.
quests.textToSpeak: I wouldn't have thought of that.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on HAV-en't, HEARD, BACK, US, YET.
quests.explanation: Negative auxiliaries take a beat, so HAV-en't, HEARD, BACK and YET carry the rhythm while 'from us' shrinks.
quests.textToSpeak: They haven't heard back from us yet.
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same bounce and timing as the model.

quests.hint: Beats on MEET, BUS, OUT-side, POST.
quests.explanation: Compound nouns such as 'bus stop' and 'post office' are stressed on the first part. That places beats on MEET, BUS, OUT-side and POST.
quests.textToSpeak: Meet me at the bus stop outside the post office.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on BIKE, be-HIND and TRAIN.
quests.explanation: 'Bike rack' and 'train station' each stress the first word, and 'behind' takes the middle beat, so the rhythm is BIKE, be-HIND, TRAIN.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a bike rack behind the train station.
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.hint: Beats on SEND, CUS-tomer, SER-vice, DESK.
quests.explanation: In the long noun phrase 'customer service desk', each part takes a beat: CUS-, SER- and DESK. 'It to the' shrinks to make room.
quests.textToSpeak: Send it to the customer service desk.
quests.instruction: Tap the beats as you listen, then repeat in the same rhythm.

quests.hint: Beats on MIND and JOINED.
quests.explanation: 'Would you' and 'if I' shrink so that MIND and JOINED carry the beats. Keeping the pattern brisk makes the request sound relaxed, not hesitant.
quests.textToSpeak: Would you mind if I joined you?
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.hint: Beats on HAP-pen, KNOW, EX-it.
quests.explanation: The opening 'do you happen to' is a soft, quick lead-in, so the beats fall on HAP-pen, KNOW and EX-it.
quests.textToSpeak: Do you happen to know where the exit is?
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on WON-dering, HELP, SOME-thing.
quests.explanation: The long lead-in 'I was wondering if you could' is quick and light, so the real request lands on HELP and SOME-thing.
quests.textToSpeak: I was wondering if you could help me with something.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the beat.

quests.hint: Beats on FIRST, O-pen, TAP, SET-tings, I-con.
quests.explanation: Instructions use a steady beat on actions and objects: FIRST, O-pen, TAP, SET-tings, I-con. Small words fit in between.
quests.textToSpeak: First, open the app; then tap the settings icon.
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on HOLD, BUT-ton, DOWN, LIGHT, GREEN.
quests.explanation: Each key word takes a beat, and 'until the' is quick. This keeps an instruction easy to follow in real time.
quests.textToSpeak: Hold the button down until the light turns green.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on FILL, FORM, SIGN, BOT-tom, HAND.
quests.explanation: Three commands make three thought groups, each with a beat on its verb: FILL, SIGN, HAND. 'Hand it in' links as 'han-di-tin'.
quests.textToSpeak: Fill in the form, sign at the bottom, and hand it in.
quests.instruction: Repeat with the same bounce and timing as the model.

quests.hint: Beats on RAINS, MOVE, e-VENT, in-SIDE.
quests.explanation: The first clause sets up a beat pattern and the second answers it. The pause after 'rains' resets the rhythm before MOVE, e-VENT and in-SIDE.
quests.textToSpeak: If it rains, we'll move the event inside.
quests.instruction: Listen once, then reproduce the rhythm of the phrase.

quests.hint: Beats on ar-RIVE, TEXT and ROOM NUM-ber.
quests.explanation: Two short clauses, each with its own beats. The pause after 'arrive' keeps them separate, and 'your' stays weak.
quests.textToSpeak: Once you arrive, text me your room number.
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.hint: Beats on MEET-ing, SEND, NOTES.
quests.explanation: 'After the' is quick and lands on MEET-ing; the pause resets the rhythm before I'll SEND the NOTES.
quests.textToSpeak: After the meeting, I'll send the notes.
quests.instruction: Tap the beats as you listen, then repeat in the same rhythm.

quests.hint: Beats on GOOD, CHANCE, RAIN, KEEP-ing, PLAN.
quests.explanation: Two contrasting clauses share a rhythm: GOOD CHANCE it'll RAIN, keeping the PLAN. 'But we're' is squeezed at the junction.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a good chance it'll rain, but we're keeping the plan.
quests.instruction: Keep the small words quick and match the pacing.

quests.hint: Beats on SAID, CALL, AF-ter-NOON, NOTH-ing, YET.
quests.explanation: The first clause has four beats and the second only two, so speed up slightly on NOTH-ing YET to show the contrast.
quests.textToSpeak: She said she'd call this afternoon, but nothing yet.
quests.instruction: Listen for the rhythm, then repeat with the same timing.

quests.hint: Beats on TRAIN, LATE, MISSED, START, FILM.
quests.explanation: Cause and effect follow the same beat pattern: TRAIN, LATE / MISSED, START, FILM. 'So we' and 'of the' are squeezed.
quests.textToSpeak: The train was late, so we missed the start of the film.
quests.instruction: Shadow the speaker and match the beat.
